claims.text: As-produced refractory HEAs are typically multiphase.
As-produced refractory HEAs are typically unoptimized with respect to activation properties.
Selecting low-activation refractory elements such as W, Cr, and V can produce a single-phase HEA.
Avoiding elements that produce long-lived radioisotopes will reduce the alloy's induced radioactivity.
Tailoring a refractory HEA to contain only low-activation refractory elements will maintain or enhance its high-temperature mechanical properties under fusion PFC conditions.
The proposed composition will form a stabilized single-phase microstructure.
The stabilized single-phase microstructure will resist irradiation-induced phase transformations.
The stabilized single-phase microstructure will minimize formation of long-lived radioisotopes.
Optimizing elemental makeup will retain a microstructure that supports high-temperature mechanical stability.
Optimizing elemental makeup will retain irradiation resistance.
The composition change will suppress deleterious phase changes under high-flux irradiation.
The optimized HEA will have statistically significantly lower post-irradiation activity than conventional tungsten-based materials or reduced-activation ferritic/martensitic steels.
The optimized HEA will maintain or improve high-temperature tensile strength relative to conventional tungsten-based materials or reduced-activation ferritic/martensitic steels.
The optimized HEA will maintain or improve high-temperature ductility relative to conventional tungsten-based materials or reduced-activation ferritic/martensitic steels.
Conventional tungsten-based materials suffer from brittleness or activation issues.
Reduced-activation ferritic/martensitic steels have limited operating-temperature ranges.
Trade-offs may exist between the optimal elemental combination and formation of brittle phases.
